B372: where:
B373: xthe first digit:
B374: 1presented to TSG for information;
B375: 2presented to TSG for approval;
B376: 3or greater indicates TSG approved document under change control.

B414: [29]3GPP TS 24.554: "Technical Specification Group Core Network and Terminals; Proximity-services (ProSe) in 5G System (5GS) protocol".
B415: [30]3GPP TS 23.586: "Technical Specification Group Services and System Aspects; Architectural Enhancements to support Ranging based services and Sidelink Positioning".
B416: [31]3GPP TS 23.256: "Support of Uncrewed Aerial Systems (UAS) connectivity, identification and tracking; Stage 2".
B417: [32]3GPP TS 23.501: "Technical Specification Group Services and System Aspects; System Architecture for the 5G System (5GS); Stage 2".
B418: 3Definitions, symbols and abbreviations
B419: 3.1Definitions
B420: For the purposes of the present document, the terms and definitions given in TR 21.905 [1] and the following apply. A term defined in the present document takes precedence over the definition of the same term, if any, in TR 21.905 [1].
B421: A2X communication: A communication to support A2X services leveraging PC5 reference points, as defined in TS 23.256 [31]. A2X services are realized by various types of A2X applications, e.g., BRID or DAA.
B422: Air to Ground network: An NG-RAN consisting of ground-based gNBs, which provide cell towers that send signals up to an aircraft's antenna(s) of onboard ATG terminal, with typical vertical altitude of around 10,000 m and take-off/landing altitudes down to 3000 m.
B423: BWP for SRS for positioning Tx frequency hopping: For SRS for positioning Tx frequency hopping, separate BWP configuration outside BWP configuration for data transmission.
B424: CLTM candidate cell: A candidate cell configured for conditional LTM as defined in TS 38.331 [5].
B425: Dedicated SL-PRS resource pool: A sidelink resource pool which can be used for the transmission of SL-PRS and cannot be used for the transmission of PSSCH.
B426: Dormant BWP: The dormant BWP is one of downlink BWPs configured by the network via dedicated RRC signaling. In the dormant BWP, the UE stop monitoring PDCCH on/for the SCell, but continues performing CSI measurements, Automatic Gain Control (AGC) and beam management, if configured.
B427: DRX group: A group of Serving Cells that is configured by RRC and that have the same DRX Active Time.
B428: eRedCap UE: A UE with enhanced reduced capabilities as specified in clause 4.2.22.1 of TS 38.306 [25].
B429: HARQ information: HARQ information for DL-SCH, for UL-SCH, or for SL-SCH transmissions consists of New Data Indicator (NDI), Transport Block Size (TBS), Redundancy Version (RV), and HARQ process ID.
B430: IAB-donor: gNB that provides network access to UEs via a network of backhaul and access links.
B431: IAB-node: RAN node that supports NR access links to UEs and NR backhaul links to parent nodes and child nodes.
B432: Listen Before Talk: A procedure according to which transmissions are not performed if the channel is identified as being occupied, see TS 37.213 [18].
B433: LTM candidate cell: A candidate cell configured for LTM as defined in TS 38.331 [5].
B434: Msg3: Message transmitted on UL-SCH containing a C-RNTI MAC CE or CCCH SDU, submitted from upper layer and associated with the UE Contention Resolution Identity, as part of a Random Access procedure.
B435: Multi-path: Mode of operation of a UE in RRC_CONNECTED configured with one direct path on which the UE connects to gNB using NR Uu, and one indirect path on which the UE connects to the same gNB via another UE using PC5 unicast link or non-3GPP connection (N3C).
B436: Multi-PUSCH configured grant: A configured grant configuration configured with nrOfSlotsInCG-Period (see TS 38.331 [5]). It includes multiple consecutive configured uplink grants within a single periodicity.
B437: N3C indirect path: In Multi-path, the indirect path using Non-3GPP Connection between a remote UE and one or more relay UE(s).
B438: NCR-Fwd: NCR-node function, which performs amplifying-and-forwarding of UL/DL RF signals between gNB and UE. The behavior of the NCR-Fwd is controlled according to the side control information received by the NCR-MT from a gNB.
B439: NCR-MT: NCR-node entity which communicates with a gNB via a control link to receive side control information. The control link is based on NR Uu interface.
B440: NCR-node: RAN node comprising NCR-MT and NCR-Fwd.
B441: Non-terrestrial network: An NG-RAN consisting of gNBs, which provide non-terrestrial NR access to UEs by means of an NTN payload embarked on an airborne or space-borne NTN vehicle and an NTN Gateway.
B442: NR backhaul link: NR link used for backhauling between an IAB-node and an IAB-donor, and between IAB-nodes in case of a multi-hop backhauling.
B443: NR sidelink communication: AS functionality enabling at least V2X Communication as defined in TS 23.287 [19] and ProSe communication (including ProSe non-Relay, single-hop UE-to-Network Relay, Multihop L2 UE-to-Network Relay, and UE-to-UE Relay communication (including ProSe UE-to-UE Relay communication with integrated discovery)) as defined in TS 23.304 [26], between two or more nearby UEs, using NR technology but not traversing any network node.
B444: NR sidelink discovery: AS functionality enabling ProSe non-Relay discovery, ProSe UE-to-Network Relay discovery, ProSe Multihop L2 UE-to-Network Relay discovery, and ProSe UE-to-UE Relay discovery for Proximity based Services as defined in TS 23.304 [26], between two or more nearby UEs, using NR technology but not traversing any network node.
B445: NR sidelink transmission: Any NR Sidelink-based transmission, including transmission for NR sidelink discovery, transmission for NR sidelink communication, transmission for Ranging/Sidelink Positioning, and transmission for A2X communication.
B446: PDCCH occasion: A time duration (i.e. one or a consecutive number of symbols) during which the MAC entity is configured to monitor the PDCCH.
B447: Positioning SRS Bandwidth Aggregation: Transmission of positioning SRS on multiple carriers in RRC_CONNECTED and RRC_INACTIVE where the positioning SRS resources are linked in RRC configuration as defined in TS 38.331 [5].
B448: PRS Processing Window: A time window during which UE may perform PRS measurement inside the active DL BWP with the same numerology as the active DL BWP without measurement gap.
B449: Ranging/Sidelink Positioning: AS functionality enabling ranging-based services and sidelink positioning as specified in TS 23.586 [30].
B450: RB set: A RB set refers to a contiguous set of resource blocks (RBs) on which a channel access procedure is performed in shared spectrum as defined in TS 37.213 [18].
B451: RedCap UE: A UE with reduced capabilities as specified in clause 4.2.21.1 in TS 38.306 [25].
B452: Serving Cell: A PCell, a PSCell, or an SCell in TS 38.331 [5].
B453: Shared SL-PRS resource pool: A sidelink resource pool which can be used for the transmission of both SL-PRS and PSSCH.
B454: Sidelink transmission information: Sidelink transmission information included in an SCI for an SL-SCH transmission or SL-PRS transmission with or without SL-SCH transmission on Shared SL-PRS resource pool as specified in clause 8.3 and 8.4 of TS 38.212 [9] consists of Sidelink HARQ information including NDI, RV, Sidelink process ID, HARQ feedback enabled/disabled indicator, Sidelink identification information including cast type indicator, Source Layer-1 ID and Destination Layer-1 ID, and Sidelink other information including CSI request, SL-PRS request, SL-PRS resource ID, a priority, a communication range requirement and Zone ID and COT sharing information.
B455: SL-PRS delay budget: Delay budget before which the SL-PRS is expected to be transmitted by the Tx UE.
B456: SL-PRS transmission information on Dedicated SL-PRS resource pool: SL-PRS transmission information on Dedicated SL-PRS resource pool is included in an SCI for an SL-PRS transmission on Dedicated SL-PRS resource pool, as specified in TS 38.212 [9], consisting of
B457: -SL-PRS identification information, including cast type indicator, source ID and destination ID;
B458: -SL-PRS transmission other information, including SL-PRS priority, SL-PRS request, SL-PRS resource ID and resource reservation period.
B459: SRS positioning validity area: An area consisting of a list of cells within which the corresponding positioning SRS configuration is considered as valid.
B460: Special Cell: For Dual Connectivity operation the term Special Cell refers to the PCell of the MCG or the PSCell of the SCG depending on if the MAC entity is associated to the MCG or the SCG, respectively. Otherwise the term Special Cell refers to the PCell. A Special Cell supports PUCCH transmission and contention-based Random Access, and is always activated.
B461: Timing Advance Group: A group of Serving Cells that is configured by RRC and that, for the cells with a UL configured, using the same timing reference cell and the same Timing Advance value. A Timing Advance Group containing the SpCell of a MAC entity is referred to as Primary Timing Advance Group (PTAG), whereas the term Secondary Timing Advance Group (STAG) refers to other TAGs.
B462: UE-gNB RTT: For non-terrestrial networks, the sum of the UE's Timing Advance value (see TS 38.211 [8] clause 4.3.1) and kmac.
B463: V2X sidelink communication: AS functionality enabling V2X Communication as defined in TS 23.285 [20], between nearby UEs, using E-UTRA technology but not traversing any network node.
B464: NOTE 1:A timer is running once it is started, until it is stopped or until it expires; otherwise it is not running. A timer can be started if it is not running or restarted if it is running. A Timer is always started or restarted from its initial value. The duration of a timer is not updated until it is stopped or expires (e.g. due to BWP switching). When the MAC entity applies zero value for a timer, the timer shall be started and immediately expire unless explicitly stated otherwise.
B465: NOTE 2:In this version of the specification, the SRS in the procedural description includes Positioning SRS except for the Positioning SRS for transmission in RRC_INACTIVE as in clause 5.26. Positioning SRS except for the Positioning SRS for transmission in RRC_INACTIVE is treated the same as SRS by the UE unless explicitly stated otherwise.

B564: 4General
B565: 4.1Introduction
B566: The objective of this clause is to describe the MAC architecture and the MAC entity of the UE from a functional point of view.
B567: 4.2MAC architecture
B568: 4.2.1General
B569: This clause describes a model of the MAC i.e. it does not specify or restrict implementations.
B570: RRC is in control of the MAC configuration.
B571: 4.2.2MAC Entities
B572: The MAC entity of the UE handles the following transport channels:
B573: -Broadcast Channel (BCH);
B574: -Downlink Shared Channel(s) (DL-SCH);
B575: -Paging Channel (PCH);
B576: -Uplink Shared Channel(s) (UL-SCH);
B577: -Random Access Channel(s) (RACH).
B578: When the UE is configured with SCG, two MAC entities are configured to the UE: one for the MCG and one for the SCG.
B579: When the UE is configured with DAPS handover, two MAC entities are used by the UE: one for the source cell (source MAC entity) and one for the target cell (target MAC entity).
B580: The functions of the different MAC entities in the UE operate independently unless otherwise specified. The timers and parameters used in each MAC entity are configured independently unless otherwise specified. The Serving Cells, C-RNTI, radio bearers, logical channels, upper and lower layer entities, LCGs, and HARQ entities considered by each MAC entity refer to those mapped to that MAC entity unless otherwise specified.
B581: If the MAC entity is configured with one or more SCells, there are multiple DL-SCH and there may be multiple UL-SCH as well as multiple RACH per MAC entity; one DL-SCH, one UL-SCH, and one RACH on the SpCell, one DL-SCH, zero or one UL-SCH and zero or one RACH for each SCell.
B582: If the MAC entity is not configured with any SCell, there is one DL-SCH, one UL-SCH, and one RACH per MAC entity.
B583: If the UE is configured with LTM candidate cell(s), there may be zero or one RACH for each LTM candidate cell, which shares the same corresponding MAC entity with Serving Cell.
B584: Figure 4.2.2-1 illustrates one possible structure of the MAC entity when SCG is not configured and for each MAC entity during DAPS handover.
B586: Figure 4.2.2-1: MAC structure overview
B587: Figure 4.2.2-2 illustrates one possible structure for the MAC entities when MCG and SCG are configured.
B589: Figure 4.2.2-2: MAC structure overview with two MAC entities
B590: In addition, the MAC entity of the UE handles the following transport channel for sidelink:
B591: -Sidelink Shared Channel (SL-SCH);
B592: -Sidelink Broadcast Channel (SL-BCH).
B593: Figure 4.2.2-3 illustrates one possible structure for the MAC entity when sidelink is configured.
B595: Figure 4.2.2-3: MAC structure overview for sidelink
B596: 4.3Services
B597: 4.3.1Services provided to upper layers
B598: The MAC sublayer provides the following services to upper layers:
B599: -data transfer;
B600: -radio resource allocation.
B601: 4.3.2Services expected from physical layer
B602: The MAC sublayer expects the following services from the physical layer:
B603: -data transfer services;
B604: -signalling of HARQ feedback;
B605: -signalling of Scheduling Request;
B606: -measurements (e.g. Channel Quality Indication (CQI)).
B607: 4.4Functions
B608: The MAC sublayer supports the following functions:
B609: -mapping between logical channels and transport channels;
B610: -multiplexing of MAC SDUs from one or different logical channels onto transport blocks (TB) to be delivered to the physical layer on transport channels;
B611: -demultiplexing of MAC SDUs to one or different logical channels from transport blocks (TB) delivered from the physical layer on transport channels;
B612: -scheduling information reporting;
B613: -error correction through HARQ;
B614: -logical channel prioritization;
B615: -priority handling between overlapping resources of one UE;
B616: -radio resource selection.
B617: The relevance of MAC functions for uplink, downlink, and sidelink is indicated in Table 4.4-1.
B618: Table 4.4-1: The link direction association of MAC functions.

B619 R1: Mapping between logical channels and transport channels | X | X | X | X
B619 R2: Multiplexing |  | X | X | 
B619 R3: Demultiplexing | X |  |  | X
B619 R4: Scheduling information reporting |  | X | X | 
B619 R5: Error correction through HARQ | X | X | X | X
B619 R6: Logical Channel  prioritization |  | X | X | 
B619 R7: Radio resource selection |  |  | X |

B654: 5MAC procedures
B655: 5.1Random Access procedure
B656: 5.1.1Random Access procedure initialization
B657: The Random Access procedure described in this clause is initiated by a PDCCH order, by the MAC entity itself, or by RRC for the events in accordance with TS 38.300 [2]. There is only one Random Access procedure ongoing at any point in time in a MAC entity. The Random Access procedure on an SCell or an LTM candidate cell shall only be initiated by a PDCCH order with ra-PreambleIndex different from 0b000000.
B658: NOTE 1:If a new Random Access procedure is triggered while another is already ongoing in the MAC entity, it is up to UE implementation whether to continue with the ongoing procedure or start with the new procedure (e.g. for SI request).
B659: NOTE 2:If there was an ongoing Random Access procedure that is triggered by a PDCCH order while the UE receives another PDCCH order for the same serving cell indicating the same Random Access Preamble, PRACH mask index and uplink carrier, the Random Access procedure is considered as the same Random Access procedure as the ongoing one and not initialized again.
B660: When a Random Access procedure is initiated, UE selects a set of Random Access resources as specified in clause 5.1.1b and initialises the following parameters for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources:
B661: -prach-ConfigurationIndex: the available set of PRACH occasions for the transmission of the Random Access Preamble for Msg1. These are also applicable to the MSGA PRACH if the PRACH occasions are shared between 2-step and 4-step RA types;
B662: -prach-ConfigurationPeriodScaling-IAB: the scaling factor defined in TS 38.211 [8] and applicable to IAB-MTs, extending the periodicity of the PRACH occasions baseline configuration indicated by prach-ConfigurationIndex;
B663: -prach-ConfigurationFrameOffset-IAB: the frame offset defined in TS 38.211 [8] and applicable to IAB-MTs, altering the ROs frame defined in the baseline configuration indicated by prach-ConfigurationIndex;
B664: -prach-ConfigurationSOffset-IAB: the subframe/slot offset defined in TS 38.211 [8] and applicable to IAB-MTs, altering the ROs subframe or slot defined in the baseline configuration indicated by prach-ConfigurationIndex;
B665: -msgA-PRACH-ConfigurationIndex: the available set of PRACH occasions for the transmission of the Random Access Preamble for MSGA in 2-step RA type;
B666: -preambleReceivedTargetPower: initial Random Access Preamble power for 4-step RA type;
B667: -sbfd-RACH-SingleConfig-preambleReceivedTargetPower: initial Random Access Preamble power for 4-step RA type associated with the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6];
B668: -msgA-PreambleReceivedTargetPower: initial Random Access Preamble power for 2-step RA type;
B669: -rsrp-ThresholdSSB: an RSRP threshold for the selection of the SSB for 4-step RA type. If the Random Access procedure is initiated for beam failure recovery, rsrp-ThresholdSSB used for the selection of the SSB within candidateBeamRSList refers to rsrp-ThresholdSSB in BeamFailureRecoveryConfig IE;
B670: -rsrp-ThresholdCSI-RS: an RSRP threshold for the selection of CSI-RS for 4-step RA type. If the Random Access procedure is initiated for beam failure recovery, rsrp-ThresholdCSI-RS is equal to rsrp-ThresholdSSB in BeamFailureRecoveryConfig IE;
B671: -msgA-RSRP-ThresholdSSB: an RSRP threshold for the selection of the SSB for 2-step RA type;
B672: -rsrp-ThresholdSSB-SUL: an RSRP threshold for the selection between the NUL carrier and the SUL carrier;
B673: -msgA-RSRP-Threshold: an RSRP threshold for selection between 2-step RA type and 4-step RA type when both 2-step and 4-step RA type Random Access Resources are configured in the UL BWP;
B674: -rsrp-ThresholdMsg1-RepetitionNum2: an RSRP threshold for Msg1 repetition with repetition number 2 (see clause 5.1.1b);
B675: -rsrp-ThresholdMsg1-RepetitionNum4: an RSRP threshold for Msg1 repetition with repetition number 4 (see clause 5.1.1b);
B676: -rsrp-ThresholdMsg1-RepetitionNum8: an RSRP threshold for Msg1 repetition with repetition number 8 (see clause 5.1.1b);
B677: -sbfd-RSRP-ThresholdMsg1-RepetitionNum2: an RSRP threshold for Msg1 repetition with repetition number 2 associated with the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6] (see clause 5.1.1b);
B678: -sbfd-RSRP-ThresholdMsg1-RepetitionNum4: an RSRP threshold for Msg1 repetition with repetition number 4 associated with the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6] (see clause 5.1.1b);
B679: -sbfd-RSRP-ThresholdMsg1-RepetitionNum8: an RSRP threshold for Msg1 repetition with repetition number 8 associated with the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6] (see clause 5.1.1b);
B680: -rsrp-ThresholdMsg3: an RSRP threshold for Msg3 repetition (see clause 5.1.1b);
B681: -sbfd-RSRP-ThresholdRO-Type: an RSRP threshold for the selection of the initial RO type between the first PRACH occasions and the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6] in contention-based Random Access procedure;
B682: -sbfd-RSRP-ThresholdRO-TypeUsage: indicates how sbfd-RSRP-ThresholdRO-Type is used in initial RO type selection;
B683: -sbfd-RO-Type: indicates the initial RO type, between the first PRACH occasions and the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6], to be used in the Random Access procedure;
B684: -sib1-RSRP-ThresholdSSB: an RSRP threshold for the selection of the SSB for SIB1 request;
B685: -FeatureCombination: feature or a combination of features associated with a set of Random Access resources;
B686: -featurePriorities: priorities for features, such as (e)RedCap, Slicing, etc. (see clause 5.1.1d);
B687: -msgA-TransMax: The maximum number of MSGA transmissions when both 4-step and 2-step RA type Random Access Resources are configured;
B688: -candidateBeamRSList: a list of reference signals (CSI-RS and/or SSB) identifying the candidate beams for recovery and the associated Random Access parameters;

B690: -powerRampingStep: the power-ramping factor;

B694: -ra-PreambleIndex: Random Access Preamble;

B696: -msgA-SSB-SharedRO-MaskIndex: Indicates the subset of 4-step RA type PRACH occasions shared with 2-step RA type PRACH occasions for each SSB. If 2-step RA type PRACH occasions are shared with 4-step RA type PRACH occasions and msgA-SSB-SharedRO-MaskIndex is not configured, then all 4-step RA type PRACH occasions are available for 2-step RA type (see clause 7.4);
B697: -ssb-SharedRO-MaskIndex: defines PRACH occasions, on which preambles are allocated for a feature or a combination of features, associated with an SSB in which the MAC entity may transmit a Random Access Preamble (see clause 7.4);

B701: -startPreambleForThisPartition: the first preamble associated with the set of Random Access Resources applicable to the Random Access procedure;
B702: -preambleTransMax: the maximum number of Random Access Preamble transmission;
B703: -preambleTransMax-Msg1-Repetition: the maximum number of Random Access Preamble transmissions with a given Msg1 repetition number before switching to Msg1 repetition with the next available higher Msg1 repetition number;
B704: -preambleTransMaxRO-Type: the maximum number of Random Access Preamble transmissions before switching RO type between the first PRACH occasions and the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6];
B705: -ssb-perRACH-OccasionAndCB-PreamblesPerSSB: defines the number of SSBs mapped to each PRACH occasion for 4-step RA type and the number of contention-based Random Access Preambles mapped to each SSB;
B706: -msgA-CB-PreamblesPerSSB-PerSharedRO: defines the number of contention-based Random Access Preambles for 2-step RA type mapped to each SSB when the PRACH occasions are shared between 2-step and 4-step RA types;
B707: -msgA-SSB-PerRACH-OccasionAndCB-PreamblesPerSSB: defines the number of SSBs mapped to each PRACH occasion for 2-step RA type and the number of contention-based Random Access Preambles mapped to each SSB;
B708: -numberOfPreamblesPerSSB-ForThisPartition: defines the number of consecutive preambles for a feature or a combination of features mapped to each SSB;
B709: -msgA-PUSCH-ResourceGroupA: defines MSGA PUSCH resources that the UE shall use when performing MSGA transmission using Random Access Preambles group A;
B710: -msgA-PUSCH-ResourceGroupB: defines MSGA PUSCH resources that the UE shall use when performing MSGA transmission using Random Access Preambles group B;
B711: -msgA-PUSCH-Resource-Index: identifies the index of the PUSCH resource used for MSGA in case of contention-free Random Access with 2-step RA type;
B712: -if groupBconfigured is configured, then Random Access Preambles group B is configured for 4-step RA type.
B713: -Amongst the contention-based Random Access Preambles associated with an SSB (as defined in TS 38.213 [6]), the first numberOfRA-PreamblesGroupA included in groupBconfigured Random Access Preambles belong to Random Access Preambles group A. The remaining Random Access Preambles associated with the SSB belong to Random Access Preambles group B (if configured).
B714: -if groupB-ConfiguredTwoStepRA is configured, then Random Access Preambles group B is configured for 2-step RA type.
B715: -Amongst the contention-based Random Access Preambles for 2-step RA type associated with an SSB (as defined in TS 38.213 [6]), the first numberOfRA-PreamblesGroupA included in GroupB-ConfiguredTwoStepRA Random Access Preambles belong to Random Access Preambles group A. The remaining Random Access Preambles associated with the SSB belong to Random Access Preambles group B (if configured).
B716: NOTE 3:If Random Access Preambles group B is supported by the cell Random Access Preambles group B is included for each SSB.
B717: -if Random Access Preambles group B is configured for 4-step RA type:

B726: -ra-MsgA-SizeGroupA: the threshold to determine the groups of Random Access Preambles for 2-step RA type.
B727: -the set of Random Access Preambles and/or PRACH occasions for SI request, if any;
B728: -the set of Random Access Preambles and/or PRACH occasions for SIB1 request, if any;

B732: -ra-ContentionResolutionTimer: the Contention Resolution Timer (SpCell only);
B733: -msgB-ResponseWindow: the time window to monitor RA response(s) for 2-step RA type (SpCell only).

B756: When the Random Access procedure is initiated on a Serving Cell or for an LTM candidate cell, the MAC entity shall:
B757: 1>flush the Msg3 buffer;
B758: 1>flush the MSGA buffer;
B759: 1>set the PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER to 1;
B760: 1>if the Random Access procedure is initiated on a Serving Cell; or
B761: 1>if the Random Access procedure is initiated by the PDCCH order for an LTM candidate cell and the PDCCH order indicates preamble initial transmission; or
B762: 1>if the Random Access procedure is initiated by the PDCCH order for an LTM candidate cell, which is different from the cell to which the MAC entity performed the last Random Access Preamble transmission, and the PDCCH order indicates preamble re-transmission:
B763: 2>set the PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER to 1;
B764: 1>set the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF to 0 ms;
B765: 1>set POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA to 0 dB;
B766: 1>set POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE to 0 dB;
B767: 1>if the carrier to use for the Random Access procedure is explicitly signalled:
B768: 2>select the signalled carrier for performing Random Access procedure;
B769: 2>set the PCMAX to PCMAX,f,c of the signalled carrier.
B770: 1>else if the carrier to use for the Random Access procedure is not explicitly signalled; and
B771: 1>if the Serving Cell for the Random Access procedure is configured with supplementary uplink as specified in TS 38.331 [5]; and
B772: 1>if the RSRP of the downlink pathloss reference is less than rsrp-ThresholdSSB-SUL:
B773: 2>select the SUL carrier for performing Random Access procedure;
B774: 2>set the PCMAX to PCMAX,f,c of the SUL carrier.
B775: 1>else:
B776: 2>select the NUL carrier for performing Random Access procedure;
B777: 2>set the PCMAX to PCMAX,f,c of the NUL carrier.
B778: NOTE 4:Void.

B798: 1>else:

B920: 5.1.1bSelection of the set of Random Access resources for the Random Access procedure
B921: The MAC entity shall:
B922: 1>if the BWP selected for Random Access procedure is configured with both set(s) of Random Access resources with msg3-Repetitions set to true and set(s) of Random Access resources without msg3-Repetitions set to true and the RSRP of the downlink pathloss reference is less than rsrp-ThresholdMsg3; or
B923: 1>if the BWP selected for Random Access procedure is only configured with the set(s) of Random Access resources with msg3-Repetitions set to true:
B924: 2>assume Msg3 repetition is applicable for the current Random Access procedure.
B925: 1>else:
B926: 2>assume Msg3 repetition is not applicable for the current Random Access procedure.
B927: 1>if contention-free Random Access Resources have been provided for this Random Access procedure in the (Enhanced) LTM Cell Switch Command MAC CE and a non-zero Msg1 repetition number is indicated in the (Enhanced) LTM Cell Switch Command MAC CE:
B928: 2>assume that Msg1 repetition is applicable and that the Msg1 repetition number applicable for the current Random Access procedure is the Msg1 repetition number indicated in the (Enhanced) LTM Cell Switch Command MAC CE.
B929: 1>else if contention-free Random Access Resources have been provided for this Random Access procedure and a Msg1 repetition number is indicated in rach-ConfigDedicated:

B1135: 5.1.1dSelection of the set of Random Access resources based on feature prioritization
B1136: The MAC entity shall:
B1137: 1>among the available sets of Random Access resources for this Random Access procedure (as specified in clause 5.1.1c), identify those configured with a feature which has the highest priority assigned in featurePriorities among all the features applicable to this Random Access procedure as specified in TS 38.331 [5].
B1138: 1>if a single set of Random Access resources is identified:
B1139: 2>select this set of Random Access resources.
B1140: 1>else if more than one set of Random Access resources is identified:
B1141: 2>if all the identified sets of Random Access resources are configured with Msg1 repetition indication and the same featureCombination:
B1142: 3>select the set of Random Access resources that associated with highest Msg1 repetition number among the identified sets of Random Access resources.
B1143: 2>else:
B1144: 3>repeat the procedure taking as an input the identified sets of Random Access resources and the feature applicable to the current Random Access procedure with the highest priority assigned in featurePriorities among all the features applicable to this Random Access procedure, except the features considered already.
B1145: 1>else (i.e. no set of Random Access resources is identified):
B1146: 2>repeat the procedure taking as an input the previous identified available sets of Random Access resources and the feature applicable to the current Random Access procedure with the highest priority assigned in featurePriorities among all the features applicable to this Random Access procedure, except the features considered already.

B1292: 5.1.3Random Access Preamble transmission
B1293: The MAC entity shall, for each Random Access Preamble:
B1294: 1>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER is greater than one; and
B1295: 1>if the notification of suspending power ramping counter has not been received from lower layers; and
B1296: 1>if LBT failure indication was not received from lower layers for the last Random Access Preamble transmission; and
B1297: 1>if SSB or CSI-RS selected is not changed from the selection in the last Random Access Preamble transmission; and
B1298: 1>if the Random Access procedure is not initiated by the PDCCH order for an LTM candidate cell:
B1299: 2>increment PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER by 1.
B1300: 1>if the Random Access procedure is initiated by the PDCCH order for an LTM candidate cell as preamble re-transmission; and
B1301: 1>if the PDCCH order indicates the same LTM candidate cell and the same SSB as the last Random Access Preamble transmission:
B1302: 2>increment PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER by 1.
B1303: 1>select the value of DELTA_PREAMBLE according to clause 7.3;
B1304: 1>if the selected PRACH occasion is of the second PRACH occasions (as defined in TS 38.213 [6]) and sbfd-RACH-SingleConfig-preambleReceivedTargetPower is configured for the Random Access Procedure:
B1305: 2>set PREAMBLE_RECEIVED_TARGET_POWER to sbfd-RACH-SingleConfig-preambleReceivedTargetPower + DELTA_PREAMBLE + (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE.
B1306: 1>else if the selected PRACH occasion is of the second PRACH occasions (as defined in TS 38.213 [6]) and sbfd-RACH-DualConfig is configured for the Random Access Procedure:
B1307: 2>set PREAMBLE_RECEIVED_TARGET_POWER to preambleReceivedTargetPower (included in the sbfd-RACH-DualConfig) + DELTA_PREAMBLE + (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE.
B1308: 1>else:
B1309: 2>set PREAMBLE_RECEIVED_TARGET_POWER to preambleReceivedTargetPower + DELTA_PREAMBLE + (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE.
B1310: 1>except for contention-free Random Access Preamble for beam failure recovery request and contention-free Random Access Preamble triggered by a PDCCH order for an LTM candidate cell, compute the RA-RNTI associated with the PRACH occasion in which the Random Access Preamble is transmitted;
B1311: 1>instruct the physical layer to transmit the Random Access Preamble using the selected PRACH occasion, corresponding RA-RNTI (if available), PREAMBLE_INDEX, and PREAMBLE_RECEIVED_TARGET_POWER.
B1312: 1>if the Random Access Procedure is triggered by a PDCCH order for an LTM candidate cell:
B1313: 2>consider this Random Access procedure completed.
B1314: 1>if LBT failure indication is received from lower layers for this Random Access Preamble transmission:
B1315: 2>if lbt-FailureRecoveryConfig is configured:
B1316: 3>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure (see clause 5.1.2).
B1317: 2>else:
B1318: 3>increment PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER by 1;
B1319: 3>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMax + 1:
B1320: 4>if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted on the SpCell:
B1321: 5>indicate a Random Access problem to upper layers;
B1322: 5>if this Random Access procedure was triggered for SI request:
B1323: 6>consider the Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1324: 4>else if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted on an SCell:
B1325: 5>consider the Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1326: 3>if the Random Access procedure is not completed:
B1327: 4>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure (see clause 5.1.2).
B1328: The RA-RNTI associated with the PRACH occasion in which the Random Access Preamble is transmitted or the RA-RNTI associated with the last valid PRACH occasion in the set of PRACH occasions (as specified in TS 38.213 [6]) for Msg1 repetition, is computed as:
B1329: RA-RNTI = 1 + s_id + 14 × t_id + 14 × 80 × f_id + 14 × 80 × 8 × ul_carrier_id
B1330: where s_id is the index of the first OFDM symbol of the PRACH occasion (0 ≤ s_id < 14), t_id is the index of the first slot of the PRACH occasion in a system frame (0 ≤ t_id < 80), where the subcarrier spacing to determine t_id is based on the value of μ specified in clause 5.3.2 in TS 38.211 [8] for μ = {0, 1, 2, 3}, and for μ = {5, 6}, t_id is the index of the 120 kHz slot in a system frame that contains the PRACH occasion (0 ≤ t_id < 80), f_id is the index of the PRACH occasion in the frequency domain (0 ≤ f_id < 8), and ul_carrier_id is the UL carrier used for Random Access Preamble transmission (0 for NUL carrier, and 1 for SUL carrier). Valid PRACH occasions (as specified in TS 38.213 [6]) configured by rach-ConfigAdapt in RACH-ConfigCommon that are in FDM with other PRACH occasions in the RACH-ConfigCommon not configured by rach-ConfigAdapt are sequentially indexed with f_id starting from msg1-FDM by increasing order of frequency.
B1331: 5.1.3aMSGA transmission
B1332: The MAC entity shall, for each MSGA:
B1333: 1>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER is greater than one; and

B1340: 1>if this is the first MSGA transmission within this Random Access procedure:
B1341: 2>if the transmission is not being made for the CCCH logical channel:
B1342: 3>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include a C-RNTI MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1343: 2>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SpCell beam failure recovery and spCell-BFR-CBRA with value true is configured:
B1344: 3>if there is at least one Serving Cell of this MAC entity configured with two BFD-RS sets:
B1345: 4>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include an Enhanced BFR MAC CE or a Truncated Enhanced BFR MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1346: 3>else:
B1347: 4>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include a BFR MAC CE or a Truncated BFR MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1348: 2>else if the Random Access procedure was initiated for beam failure recovery of both BFD-RS sets of SpCell:
B1349: 3>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include an Enhanced BFR MAC CE or a Truncated Enhanced BFR MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1350: 2>obtain the MAC PDU to transmit from the Multiplexing and assembly entity according to the HARQ information determined for the MSGA payload (see clause 5.1.2a) and store it in the MSGA buffer.
B1351: 1>compute the MSGB-RNTI associated with the PRACH occasion in which the Random Access Preamble is transmitted;
B1352: 1>instruct the physical layer to transmit the MSGA using the selected PRACH occasion and the associated PUSCH resource of MSGA (if the selected preamble and PRACH occasion is mapped to a valid PUSCH occasion), using the corresponding RA-RNTI, MSGB-RNTI, PREAMBLE_INDEX, PREAMBLE_RECEIVED_TARGET_POWER, msgA-PreambleReceivedTargetPower, and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest MSGA preamble transmission (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP);
B1353: 1>if LBT failure indication is received from lower layers for the transmission of this MSGA Random Access Preamble:
B1354: 2>instruct the physical layer to cancel the transmission of the MSGA payload on the associated PUSCH resource;
B1355: 2>if lbt-FailureRecoveryConfig is configured:
B1356: 3>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure for 2-step RA type (see clause 5.1.2a).
B1357: 2>else:
B1358: 3>increment PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER by 1;
B1359: 3>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMax + 1:
B1360: 4>indicate a Random Access problem to upper layers;
B1361: 4>if this Random Access procedure was triggered for SI request:
B1362: 5>consider this Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1363: 3>if the Random Access procedure is not completed:
B1364: 4>if msgA-TransMax is applied (see clause 5.1.1a) and PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = msgA-TransMax + 1:
B1365: 5>set the RA_TYPE to 4-stepRA;
B1366: 5>perform initialization of variables specific to Random Access type as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1367: 5>if the Msg3 buffer is empty:
B1368: 6>obtain the MAC PDU to transmit from the MSGA buffer and store it in the Msg3 buffer;
B1369: 5>flush HARQ buffer used for the transmission of MAC PDU in the MSGA buffer;
B1370: 5>discard explicitly signalled contention-free 2-step RA type Random Access Resources, if any;
B1371: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure as specified in clause 5.1.2.
B1372: 4>else:
B1373: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure for 2-step RA type (see clause 5.1.2a).
B1374: NOTE:The MSGA transmission includes the transmission of the PRACH Preamble as well as the contents of the MSGA buffer in the PUSCH resource corresponding to the selected PRACH occasion and PREAMBLE_INDEX (see TS 38.213 [6])
B1375: The MSGB-RNTI associated with the PRACH occasion in which the Random Access Preamble is transmitted, is computed as:
B1376: MSGB-RNTI = 1 + s_id + 14 × t_id + 14 × 80 × f_id + 14 × 80 × 8 × ul_carrier_id + 14 × 80 × 8 × 2
B1377: where s_id is the index of the first OFDM symbol of the PRACH occasion (0 ≤ s_id < 14), t_id is the index of the first slot of the PRACH occasion in a system frame (0 ≤ t_id < 80), where the subcarrier spacing to determine t_id is based on the value of μ specified in clause 5.3.2 in TS 38.211 [8] for μ = {0, 1, 2, 3}, and for μ = {5, 6}, t_id is the index of the 120 kHz slot in a system frame that contains the PRACH occasion (0 ≤ t_id < 80), f_id is the index of the PRACH occasion in the frequency domain (0 ≤ f_id < 8), and ul_carrier_id is the UL carrier used for Random Access Preamble transmission (0 for NUL carrier, and 1 for SUL carrier). The RA-RNTI is calculated as specified in clause 5.1.3.
B1378: 5.1.4Random Access Response reception
B1379: Once the Random Access Preamble is transmitted and regardless of the possible occurrence of a measurement gap, the MAC entity shall:
B1380: 1>if the contention-free Random Access Preamble for beam failure recovery request was transmitted by the MAC entity:
B1381: 2>if the contention-free Random Access Preamble for beam failure recovery request was transmitted on a non-terrestrial network:
B1382: 3>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in BeamFailureRecoveryConfig at the PDCCH occasion as specified in TS 38.213 [6].
B1383: 2>else:
B1384: 3>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in BeamFailureRecoveryConfig at the first PDCCH occasion as specified in TS 38.213 [6] from the end of the Random Access Preamble transmission.
B1385: 2>monitor for a PDCCH transmission on the search space indicated by recoverySearchSpaceId of the SpCell identified by the C-RNTI while ra-ResponseWindow is running.
B1386: 1>else:
B1387: 2>if the Random Access Preamble was transmitted on a non-terrestrial network:
B1388: 3>if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions:
B1389: 4>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in RACH-ConfigCommon at the PDCCH occasion from the end of all repetitions of the Random Access Preamble transmission as specified in TS 38.213 [6].
B1390: 3>else:
B1391: 4>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in RACH-ConfigCommon at the PDCCH occasion as specified in TS 38.213 [6].
B1392: 2>else if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions:
B1393: 3>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in RACH-ConfigCommon at the first PDCCH occasion from the end of all repetitions of the Random Access Preamble transmission as specified in TS 38.213 [6].
B1394: 2>else if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted for SIB1 request:
B1395: 3>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in RACH-ConfigSIB1 at the first PDCCH occasion from the end of the Random Access Preamble transmission as specified in TS 38.213 [6].
B1396: 2>else:
B1397: 3>start the ra-ResponseWindow configured in RACH-ConfigCommon at the first PDCCH occasion as specified in TS 38.213 [6] from the end of the Random Access Preamble transmission.
B1398: 2>monitor the PDCCH of the SpCell for Random Access Response(s) identified by the RA-RNTI while the ra-ResponseWindow is running.
B1399: 1>if notification of a reception of a PDCCH transmission on the search space indicated by recoverySearchSpaceId is received from lower layers on the Serving Cell where the preamble was transmitted; and
B1400: 1>if PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI; and
B1401: 1>if the contention-free Random Access Preamble for beam failure recovery request was transmitted by the MAC entity:
B1402: 2>consider the Random Access procedure successfully completed.
B1403: 1>else if a valid (as specified in TS 38.213 [6]) downlink assignment has been received on the PDCCH for the RA-RNTI and the received TB is successfully decoded:
B1404: 2>if the Random Access Response contains a MAC subPDU with Backoff Indicator:
B1405: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SIB1 request:
B1406: 4>set the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF to 0 ms.
B1407: 3>else:
B1408: 4>set the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF to value of the BI field of the MAC subPDU using Table 7.2-1, multiplied with SCALING_FACTOR_BI.
B1409: 2>else:
B1410: 3>set the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF to 0 ms.
B1411: 2>if the Random Access Response contains a MAC subPDU with Random Access Preamble identifier corresponding to the transmitted PREAMBLE_INDEX (see clause 5.1.3):
B1412: 3>consider this Random Access Response reception successful.
B1413: 2>if the Random Access Response reception is considered successful:
B1414: 3>if the Random Access Response includes a MAC subPDU with RAPID only:
B1415: 4>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed;
B1416: 4>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SIB1 request:
B1417: 5>indicate the reception of an acknowledgement for SIB1 request to upper layers.
B1418: 4>else if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SI request:
B1419: 5>indicate the reception of an acknowledgement for SI request to upper layers.
B1420: 3>else:
B1421: 4>apply the following actions for the Serving Cell where the Random Access Preamble was transmitted:
B1422: 5>process the received Timing Advance Command (see clause 5.2);
B1423: 5>if the received UL grant indicates that the corresponding PUSCH transmission is in SBFD symbols as specified in clause 11.1 of TS 38.213 [6]:
B1424: 6>if sbfd-RACH-SingleConfig (see TS 38.331 [5]) is configured for the Random Access procedure:
B1425: 7>indicate the sbfd-RACH-SingleConfig-preambleReceivedTargetPower if configured, or the preambleReceivedTargetPower otherwise, and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest Random Access Preamble transmission to lower layers (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE).
B1426: 6>else if sbfd-RACH-DualConfig (see TS 38.331 [5]) is configured for the Random Access procedure:
B1427: 7>indicate the preambleReceivedTargetPower included in the sbfd-RACH-DualConfig, and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest Random Access Preamble transmission to lower layers (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE).
B1428: 6>else:
B1429: 7>indicate the preambleReceivedTargetPower and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest Random Access Preamble transmission to lower layers (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE).
B1430: 5>else (i.e., the received UL grant indicates that the corresponding PUSCH transmission is in non-SBFD symbols as specified in clause 11.1 of TS 38.213 [6]):
B1431: 6>indicate the preambleReceivedTargetPower configured for the first PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6], and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest Random Access Preamble transmission to lower layers (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP + POWER_OFFSET_2STEP_RA + POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE).
B1432: 5>if the Random Access procedure for an SCell is performed on uplink carrier where pusch-Config is not configured:
B1433: 6>ignore the received UL grant.
B1434: 5>else:
B1435: 6>process the received UL grant value and indicate it to the lower layers.
B1436: 4>if the Random Access Preamble was not selected by the MAC entity among the contention-based Random Access Preamble(s):
B1437: 5>consider the Random Access procedure successfully completed.
B1438: 4>else:
B1439: 5>set the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI to the value received in the Random Access Response;
B1440: 5>if this is the first successfully received Random Access Response within this Random Access procedure:
B1441: 6>if the transmission is not being made for the CCCH logical channel:
B1442: 7>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include a C-RNTI MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1443: 6>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SpCell beam failure recovery and spCell-BFR-CBRA with value true is configured:
B1444: 7>if there is at least one Serving Cell of this MAC entity configured with two BFD-RS sets:
B1445: 8>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include an Enhanced BFR MAC CE or a Truncated Enhanced BFR MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1446: 7>else:
B1447: 8>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include a BFR MAC CE or a Truncated BFR MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1448: 6>else if the Random Access procedure was initiated for beam failure recovery of both BFD-RS sets of SpCell:
B1449: 7>indicate to the Multiplexing and assembly entity to include an Enhanced BFR MAC CE or a Truncated Enhanced BFR MAC CE in the subsequent uplink transmission.
B1450: 6>obtain the MAC PDU to transmit from the Multiplexing and assembly entity and store it in the Msg3 buffer.
B1451: NOTE 1:If within a Random Access procedure, an uplink grant provided in the Random Access Response for the same group of contention-based Random Access Preambles has a different size than the first uplink grant allocated during that Random Access procedure, the UE behavior is not defined.
B1452: 1>if ra-ResponseWindow configured in BeamFailureRecoveryConfig expires and if a PDCCH transmission on the search space indicated by recoverySearchSpaceId addressed to the C-RNTI has not been received on the Serving Cell where the preamble was transmitted; or
B1453: 1>if ra-ResponseWindow configured in RACH-ConfigCommon or RACH-ConfigSIB1 expires, and if the Random Access Response containing Random Access Preamble identifiers that matches the transmitted PREAMBLE_INDEX has not been received:
B1454: 2>consider the Random Access Response reception not successful;
B1455: 2>increment PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER by 1;
B1456: 2>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMax + 1:
B1457: 3>if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted on the SpCell:
B1458: 4>indicate a Random Access problem to upper layers;
B1459: 4>if this Random Access procedure was triggered for SI request or SIB1 request:
B1460: 5>consider the Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1461: 3>else if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted on an SCell:
B1462: 4>consider the Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1463: 2>if the Random Access procedure is not completed:
B1464: 3>if preambleTransMaxRO-Type is applied, and neither contention-free Random Access Resources nor Random Access resources for SI request have been provided for this Random Access procedure, and PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMaxRO-Type + 1:
B1465: 4>if the RO_TYPE is set to 2nd-RO, and set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same or higher Msg1 repetition number (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), than the current set of Random Access resources, is available for the first PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6]:
B1466: 5>set the RO_TYPE to 1st-RO;
B1467: 5>select the set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same Msg1 repetition number if available, or with the next higher Msg1 repetition number otherwise (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), for this Random Access procedure;
B1468: 5>if sbfd-RACH-DualConfig is configured for the Random Access procedure (see TS 38.331 [5]):
B1469: 6>set PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP to PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP;
B1470: 6>(re-)initialize the parameters specified in clause 5.1.1 for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources;
B1471: 6>re-initialize PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP and SCALING_FACTOR_BI as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1472: 6>set POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE to (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × (PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP – PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP).
B1473: 4>else if the RO_TYPE is set to 1st-RO, and set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same or higher Msg1 repetition number (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), than the current set of Random Access resources, is available for the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6]:
B1474: 5>set the RO_TYPE to 2nd-RO;
B1475: 5>select the set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same Msg1 repetition number if available, or with the next higher Msg1 repetition number otherwise (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), for this Random Access procedure;
B1476: 5>if sbfd-RACH-DualConfig is configured for the Random Access procedure (see TS 38.331 [5]):
B1477: 6>set PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP to PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP;
B1478: 6>(re-)initialize the parameters specified in clause 5.1.1 for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources;
B1479: 6>re-initialize PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP and SCALING_FACTOR_BI as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1480: 6>set POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE to (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × (PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP – PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP).
B1481: 3>if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions and neither contention-free Random Access Resources nor Random Access resources for SI request have been provided for this Random Access procedure:
B1482: 4>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = [preambleTransMax-Msg1-Repetition] + 1; or
B1483: 4>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = 2 × [preambleTransMax-Msg1-Repetition] + 1:
B1484: 5>if set of Random Access resources configured with the same prach-ConfigurationIndex and associated with a higher Msg1 repetition number with the same feature or feature combination as the current set of Random Access resources is available:
B1485: 6>select the set of Random Access resources associated with the next higher Msg1 repetition number with the same feature or feature combination for this Random Access procedure;
B1486: 6>initialize startPreambleForThisPartition, numberOfPreamblesPerSSB-ForThisPartition, numberOfRA-PreamblesGroupA and msg1-RepetitionTimeOffsetROGroup parameters for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources.
B1487: 3>select a random backoff time according to a uniform distribution between 0 and the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF;
B1488: 3>if the criteria (as defined in clause 5.1.2) to select contention-free Random Access Resources is met during the backoff time:
B1489: 4>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure (see clause 5.1.2).
B1490: 3>else if the Random Access procedure for an SCell is performed on uplink carrier where pusch-Config is not configured:
B1491: 4>delay the subsequent Random Access transmission until the Random Access Procedure is triggered by a PDCCH order with the same ra-PreambleIndex, ra-ssb-OccasionMaskIndex, and UL/SUL indicator TS 38.212 [9].
B1492: 3>else:
B1493: 4>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure (see clause 5.1.2) after the backoff time.
B1494: The MAC entity may stop ra-ResponseWindow (and hence monitoring for Random Access Response(s)) after successful reception of a Random Access Response containing Random Access Preamble identifiers that matches the transmitted PREAMBLE_INDEX.
B1495: HARQ operation is not applicable to the Random Access Response reception.
B1496: NOTE 2:For the case that RAR PDSCH bandwidth is larger than the bandwidth the eRedCap UE can receive or process per slot, and the UL grant in RAR indicates that the time is not enough for Msg3 transmission, as specified in TS 38.213 [6], it is up to UE implementation, e.g. either to consider the Random Access Response reception not successful, or transmit Msg3.
B1497: 5.1.4aMSGB reception and contention resolution for 2-step RA type
B1498: Once the MSGA preamble is transmitted, regardless of the possible occurrence of a measurement gap, the MAC entity shall:
B1499: 1>start the msgB-ResponseWindow at the PDCCH occasion as specified in TS 38.213 [6], clause 8.2A;
B1500: 1>monitor the PDCCH of the SpCell for a Random Access Response identified by MSGB-RNTI while the msgB-ResponseWindow is running;
B1501: 1>if C-RNTI MAC CE was included in the MSGA:
B1502: 2>monitor the PDCCH of the SpCell for Random Access Response identified by the C-RNTI while the msgB-ResponseWindow is running.
B1503: 1>if notification of a reception of a PDCCH transmission of the SpCell is received from lower layers:
B1504: 2>if the C-RNTI MAC CE was included in MSGA:
B1505: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SpCell beam failure recovery or for beam failure recovery of both BFD-RS sets of SpCell (as specified in clause 5.17) and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI; or
B1506: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SDT beam failure recovery (as specified in clause 5.27.1) and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI:
B1507: 4>consider this Random Access Response reception successful;
B1508: 4>stop the msgB-ResponseWindow;
B1509: 4>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed.
B1510: 3>else if the timeAlignmentTimer associated with at least one PTAG is running; or
B1511: 3>if CG-SDT procedure is ongoing and cg-SDT-TimeAlignmentTimer is running:
B1512: 4>if the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI and contains a UL grant for a new transmission:
B1513: 5>consider this Random Access Response reception successful;
B1514: 5>stop the msgB-ResponseWindow;
B1515: 5>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed.
B1516: 3>else:
B1517: 4>if a downlink assignment has been received on the PDCCH for the C-RNTI and the received TB is successfully decoded:
B1518: 5>if the MAC PDU contains the Absolute Timing Advance Command MAC CE:
B1519: 6>process the received Timing Advance Command (see clause 5.2);
B1520: 6>consider this Random Access Response reception successful;
B1521: 6>stop the msgB-ResponseWindow;
B1522: 6>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed and finish the disassembly and demultiplexing of the MAC PDU.
B1523: 2>if a valid (as specified in TS 38.213 [6]) downlink assignment has been received on the PDCCH for the MSGB-RNTI and the received TB is successfully decoded:
B1524: 3>if the MSGB contains a MAC subPDU with Backoff Indicator:
B1525: 4>set the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF to value of the BI field of the MAC subPDU using Table 7.2-1, multiplied with SCALING_FACTOR_BI.
B1526: 3>else:
B1527: 4>set the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF to 0 ms.
B1528: 3>if the MSGB contains a fallbackRAR MAC subPDU; and
B1529: 3>if the Random Access Preamble identifier in the MAC subPDU matches the transmitted PREAMBLE_INDEX (see clause 5.1.3a):
B1530: 4>consider this Random Access Response reception successful;
B1531: 4>apply the following actions for the SpCell:
B1532: 5>process the received Timing Advance Command (see clause 5.2);
B1533: 5>indicate the msgA-PreambleReceivedTargetPower and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest Random Access Preamble transmission to lower layers (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP);
B1534: 5>if the Random Access Preamble was not selected by the MAC entity among the contention-based Random Access Preamble(s):
B1535: 6>consider the Random Access procedure successfully completed;
B1536: 6>process the received UL grant value and indicate it to the lower layers.
B1537: 5>else:
B1538: 6>set the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI to the value received in the Random Access Response;
B1539: 6>if the Msg3 buffer is empty:
B1540: 7>obtain the MAC PDU to transmit from the MSGA buffer and store it in the Msg3 buffer;
B1541: 6>process the received UL grant value and indicate it to the lower layers and proceed with Msg3 transmission.
B1542: NOTE:If within a 2-step RA type procedure, an uplink grant provided in the fallback RAR has a different size than the MSGA payload, the UE behavior is not defined.
B1543: 3>else if the MSGB contains a successRAR MAC subPDU; and
B1544: 3>if the CCCH SDU was included in the MSGA and the UE Contention Resolution Identity in the MAC subPDU matches the CCCH SDU:
B1545: 4>stop msgB-ResponseWindow;
B1546: 4>if this Random Access procedure was initiated for SI request:
B1547: 5>indicate the reception of an acknowledgement for SI request to upper layers.
B1548: 4>else:
B1549: 5>set the C-RNTI to the value received in the successRAR;
B1550: 5>apply the following actions for the SpCell:
B1551: 6>process the received Timing Advance Command (see clause 5.2);
B1552: 6>indicate the msgA-PreambleReceivedTargetPower and the amount of power ramping applied to the latest Random Access Preamble transmission to lower layers (i.e. (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP).
B1553: 4>deliver the TPC, PUCCH resource Indicator, ChannelAccess-CPext (if indicated), and HARQ feedback Timing Indicator received in successRAR to lower layers.
B1554: 4>consider this Random Access Response reception successful;
B1555: 4>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed;
B1556: 4>finish the disassembly and demultiplexing of the MAC PDU.
B1557: 1>if msgB-ResponseWindow expires, and the Random Access Response Reception has not been considered as successful based on descriptions above:
B1558: 2>increment PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER by 1;
B1559: 2>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMax + 1:
B1560: 3>indicate a Random Access problem to upper layers;
B1561: 3>if this Random Access procedure was triggered for SI request:
B1562: 4>consider this Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1563: 2>if the Random Access procedure is not completed:
B1564: 3>if msgA-TransMax is applied (see clause 5.1.1a) and PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = msgA-TransMax + 1:
B1565: 4>set the RA_TYPE to 4-stepRA;
B1566: 4>perform initialization of variables specific to Random Access type as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1567: 4>if the Msg3 buffer is empty:
B1568: 5>obtain the MAC PDU to transmit from the MSGA buffer and store it in the Msg3 buffer;
B1569: 4>flush HARQ buffer used for the transmission of MAC PDU in the MSGA buffer;
B1570: 4>discard explicitly signalled contention-free 2-step RA type Random Access Resources, if any;
B1571: 4>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure as specified in clause 5.1.2.
B1572: 3>else:
B1573: 4>select a random backoff time according to a uniform distribution between 0 and the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF;
B1574: 4>if the criteria (as defined in clause 5.1.2a) to select contention-free Random Access Resources is met during the backoff time:
B1575: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure for 2-step RA type Random Access (see clause 5.1.2a).
B1576: 4>else:
B1577: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure for 2-step RA type Random Access (see clause 5.1.2a) after the backoff time.
B1578: Upon receiving a fallbackRAR, the MAC entity may stop msgB-ResponseWindow once the Random Access Response reception is considered as successful.
B1579: 5.1.5Contention Resolution
B1580: Once Msg3 is transmitted the MAC entity shall:
B1581: 1>if the Msg3 transmission (i.e. initial transmission or HARQ retransmission) is scheduled with PUSCH repetition Type A:
B1582: 2>if Msg3 is transmitted on a non-terrestrial network:
B1583: 3>start or restart the ra-ContentionResolutionTimer in the first symbol after the end of all repetitions of the Msg3 transmission plus the UE-gNB RTT.
B1584: 2>else:
B1585: 3>start or restart the ra-ContentionResolutionTimer in the first symbol after the end of all repetitions of the Msg3 transmission.
B1586: 1>else if Msg3 transmission (i.e. initial transmission or HARQ retransmission) is transmitted on a non-terrestrial network:
B1587: 2>start or restart the ra-ContentionResolutionTimer in the first symbol after the end of the Msg3 transmission plus the UE-gNB RTT.
B1588: 1>else:
B1589: 2>start or restart the ra-ContentionResolutionTimer in the first symbol after the end of the Msg3 transmission.
B1590: 1>monitor the PDCCH while the ra-ContentionResolutionTimer is running regardless of the possible occurrence of a measurement gap;
B1591: 1>if notification of a reception of a PDCCH transmission of the SpCell is received from lower layers:
B1592: 2>if the C-RNTI MAC CE was included in Msg3:
B1593: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SpCell beam failure recovery or for beam failure recovery of both BFD-RS sets of SpCell (as specified in clause 5.17) and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI; or
B1594: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated by a PDCCH order and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI; or
B1595: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated for SDT beam failure recovery (as specified in clause 5.27.1) and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI; or
B1596: 3>if the Random Access procedure was initiated by the MAC sublayer itself or by the RRC sublayer and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to the C-RNTI and contains a UL grant for a new transmission:
B1597: 4>consider this Contention Resolution successful;
B1598: 4>stop ra-ContentionResolutionTimer;
B1599: 4>discard the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1600: 4>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed.
B1601: 2>else if the CCCH SDU was included in Msg3 and the PDCCH transmission is addressed to its TEMPORARY_C-RNTI:
B1602: 3>if the MAC PDU is successfully decoded:
B1603: 4>stop ra-ContentionResolutionTimer;
B1604: 4>if the MAC PDU contains a UE Contention Resolution Identity MAC CE; and
B1605: 4>if the UE Contention Resolution Identity in the MAC CE matches the CCCH SDU transmitted in Msg3:
B1606: 5>consider this Contention Resolution successful and finish the disassembly and demultiplexing of the MAC PDU;
B1607: 5>if this Random Access procedure was initiated for SI request:
B1608: 6>indicate the reception of an acknowledgement for SI request to upper layers.
B1609: 5>else:
B1610: 6>set the C-RNTI to the value of the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1611: 5>discard the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1612: 5>consider this Random Access procedure successfully completed.
B1613: 4>else:
B1614: 5>discard the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1615: 5>consider this Contention Resolution not successful and discard the successfully decoded MAC PDU.
B1616: 3>else, for eRedCap UE, if lower layer detects that PDSCH transmission scheduled by PDCCH has a larger bandwidth than UE can receive or process per slot:
B1617: 4>stop ra-ContentionResolutionTimer;
B1618: 4>discard the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1619: 4>consider this Contention Resolution not successful.
B1620: 1>if ra-ContentionResolutionTimer expires:
B1621: 2>if Msg3 transmission was transmitted on a non-terrestrial network:
B1622: 3>if no PDCCH addressed to TC-RNTI indicating uplink grant for a Msg3 retransmission is received after the start of the ra-ContentionResolutionTimer:
B1623: 4>discard the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1624: 4>consider the Contention Resolution not successful.
B1625: 2>else:
B1626: 3>discard the TEMPORARY_C-RNTI;
B1627: 3>consider the Contention Resolution not successful.
B1628: 1>if the Contention Resolution is considered not successful:
B1629: 2>flush the HARQ buffer used for transmission of the MAC PDU in the Msg3 buffer;
B1630: 2>increment PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER by 1;
B1631: 2>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMax + 1:
B1632: 3>indicate a Random Access problem to upper layers.
B1633: 3>if this Random Access procedure was triggered for SI request:
B1634: 4>consider the Random Access procedure unsuccessfully completed.
B1635: 2>if the Random Access procedure is not completed:
B1636: 3>if the RA_TYPE is set to 4-stepRA:
B1637: 4>if preambleTransMaxRO-Type is applied, and contention-free Random Access Resources have not been provided for this Random Access procedure, and PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = preambleTransMaxRO-Type + 1:
B1638: 5>if the RO_TYPE is set to 2nd-RO, and set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same or higher Msg1 repetition number (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), than the current set of Random Access resources, is available for the first PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6]:
B1639: 6>set the RO_TYPE to 1st-RO;
B1640: 6>select the set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same Msg1 repetition number if available, or with the next higher Msg1 repetition number otherwise (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), for this Random Access procedure;
B1641: 6>if sbfd-RACH-DualConfig is configured for the Random Access procedure (see TS 38.331 [5]):
B1642: 7>set PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP to PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP;
B1643: 7>(re-)initialize the parameters specified in clause 5.1.1 for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources;
B1644: 7>re-initialize PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP and SCALING_FACTOR_BI as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1645: 7>set POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE to (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × (PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP – PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP).
B1646: 5>else if the RO_TYPE is set to 1st-RO, and set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same or higher Msg1 repetition number (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), than the current set of Random Access resources, is available for the second PRACH occasions as defined in TS 38.213 [6]:
B1647: 6>set the RO_TYPE to 2nd-RO;
B1648: 6>select the set of Random Access resources associated with the same feature or feature combination, and with the same Msg1 repetition number if available, or with the next higher Msg1 repetition number otherwise (if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions), for this Random Access procedure;
B1649: 6>if sbfd-RACH-DualConfig is configured for the Random Access procedure (see TS 38.331 [5]):
B1650: 7>set PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP to PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP;
B1651: 7>(re-)initialize the parameters specified in clause 5.1.1 for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources;
B1652: 7>re-initialize PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP and SCALING_FACTOR_BI as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1653: 7>set POWER_OFFSET_RO_TYPE to (PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_COUNTER – 1) × (PREVIOUS_RO_TYPE_PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP – PREAMBLE_POWER_RAMPING_STEP).
B1654: 4>if the Random Access Preamble is transmitted with repetitions and contention-free Random Access Resources have not been provided for this Random Access procedure:
B1655: 5>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = [preambleTransMax-Msg1-Repetition] + 1; or
B1656: 5>if PREAMBLE_TRANSMISSION_COUNTER = 2 × [preambleTransMax-Msg1-Repetition] + 1:
B1657: 6>if set of Random Access resources configured with the same prach-ConfigurationIndex and associated with a higher Msg1 repetition number with the same feature or feature combination as the current set of Random Access resources is available:
B1658: 7>select the set of Random Access resources associated with the next higher Msg1 repetition number with the same feature or feature combination for this Random Access procedure;
B1659: 7>initialize startPreambleForThisPartition, numberOfPreamblesPerSSB-ForThisPartition, numberOfRA-PreamblesGroupA and msg1-RepetitionTimeOffsetROGroup parameters for the Random Access procedure according to the values configured by RRC for the selected set of Random Access resources.
B1660: 4>select a random backoff time according to a uniform distribution between 0 and the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF;
B1661: 4>if the criteria (as defined in clause 5.1.2) to select contention-free Random Access Resources is met during the backoff time:
B1662: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure (see clause 5.1.2);
B1663: 4>else:
B1664: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure (see clause 5.1.2) after the backoff time.
B1665: 3>else (i.e. the RA_TYPE is set to 2-stepRA):

B1668: 5>perform initialization of variables specific to Random Access type as specified in clause 5.1.1a;
B1669: 5>flush HARQ buffer used for the transmission of MAC PDU in the MSGA buffer;
B1670: 5>discard explicitly signalled contention-free 2-step RA type Random Access Resources, if any;
B1671: 5>perform the Random Access Resource selection as specified in clause 5.1.2.
B1672: 4>else:
B1673: 5>select a random backoff time according to a uniform distribution between 0 and the PREAMBLE_BACKOFF;
B1674: 5>if the criteria (as defined in clause 5.1.2a) to select contention-free Random Access Resources is met during the backoff time:
B1675: 6>perform the Random Access Resource selection procedure for 2-step RA type as specified in clause 5.1.2a.
B1676: 5>else:
B1677: 6>perform the Random Access Resource selection for 2-step RA type procedure (see clause 5.1.2a) after the backoff time.
B1678: 5.1.6Completion of the Random Access procedure
B1679: Upon completion of the Random Access procedure, the MAC entity shall:
B1680: 1>discard any explicitly signalled contention-free Random Access Resources for 2-step RA type and 4-step RA type except the 4-step RA type contention-free Random Access Resources for beam failure recovery request, if any;
B1681: 1>flush the HARQ buffer used for transmission of the MAC PDU in the Msg3 buffer and the MSGA buffer.
B1682: Upon successful completion of the Random Access procedure initiated for DAPS handover, the target MAC entity shall:
B1683: 1>indicate the successful completion of the Random Access procedure to the upper layers.
B1684: Upon successful completion of the Random Access procedure initiated for LTM cell switch, the MAC entity shall:
B1685: 1>indicate the successful completion of the LTM cell switch to upper layers.
B1686: 5.2Maintenance of Uplink Time Alignment
B1687: RRC configures the following parameters for the maintenance of UL time alignment:
B1688: -timeAlignmentTimer (per TAG) which controls how long the MAC entity considers the Serving Cells to the associated TAG to be uplink time aligned for the TAG;
B1689: -inactivePosSRS-TimeAlignmentTimer which controls how long the MAC entity considers the Positioning SRS transmission in RRC_INACTIVE in clause 5.26 to be uplink time aligned;
B1690: -cg-SDT-TimeAlignmentTimer which controls how long the MAC entity considers the uplink transmission for CG-SDT to be uplink time aligned;
B1691: -inactivePosSRS-ValidityAreaTAT which controls how long the MAC entity considers Positioning SRS transmission in RRC_INACTIVE in clause 5.26 to be uplink time aligned when SRS positioning validity area is configured;
B1692: -ltm-TimeAlignmentTimer which controls how long the MAC entity considers the CLTM candidate cell associated with this timer to be uplink time aligned. Each ltm-TimeAlignmentTimer is associated with one CLTM candidate cell;
B1693: -ltm-TimeAlignmentTimerTag2 which controls how long the MAC entity considers the CLTM candidate cell associated with this timer to be uplink time aligned for TAG with ID tag2-Id. This timer is configured if two TAGs are configured for the CLTM candidate cell.

B1828: When the MAC entity stops uplink transmissions for an SCell not configured with two TAGs due to the fact that the maximum uplink transmission timing difference between TAGs of the MAC entity or the maximum uplink transmission timing difference between TAGs of any MAC entity of the UE is exceeded, the MAC entity considers the timeAlignmentTimer associated with the SCell as expired.
B1829: When the MAC entity stops uplink transmissions associated to a STAG for an SCell configured with two TAGs due to the fact that the maximum uplink transmission timing difference between TAGs of the MAC entity or the maximum uplink transmission timing difference between TAGs of any MAC entity of the UE is exceeded, the MAC entity considers the timeAlignmentTimer associated with the STAG as expired.

Furthermore, when the timeAlignmentTimer(s) associated with all PTAG(s) is not running, CG-SDT procedure is not ongoing and Positioning SRS transmission in RRC_INACTIVE as in clause 5.26 is not ongoing, the MAC entity shall not perform any uplink transmission on any Serving Cell except the Random Access Preamble and MSGA transmission on the SpCell. The MAC entity shall not perform any uplink transmission except the Random Access Preamble and MSGA transmission when the cg-SDT-TimeAlignmentTimer is not running during the ongoing CG-SDT procedure as triggered in clause 5.27 and the inactivePosSRS-TimeAlignmentTimer or inactivePosSRS-ValidityAreaTAT is not running.
B1831: The MAC entity shall not perform any uplink transmission except the Random Access Preamble and MSGA transmission on a Serving Cell using TCI state(s) associated with a TAG for which the timeAlignmentTimer is not running. For multi-panel SDM scheme (i.e., multipanelSchemeSDM as specified in TS 38.331 [5]), the MAC entity shall not perform any PUSCH transmission on a Serving Cell if any TCI state to be used for the multi-panel SDM transmission is associated with a TAG for which the timeAlignmentTimer is not running.
B1832: The MAC entity shall not transmit any UE Initiated Report Indication on PUCCH for a mode-B UE-initiated CSI report configured for a Serving Cell (configured by CSI-ReportConfig as specified in TS 38.331 [5]) that belongs to a TAG for which the timeAlignmentTimer is not running.
B1833: 5.2aMaintenance of UL Synchronization
B1834: The MAC entity shall for each Serving Cell:
B1835: 1>if an indication of uplink synchronization has been received from upper layers (see clauses 5.2.2.6 and 5.7.19 of TS 38.331 [5]):
B1836: 2>if indication of uplink synchronization is received after indication of uplink synchronization loss due to satellite switch with re-synchronization (see clause 5.7.19 of TS 38.331 [5]):
B1837: 3>set NTA value (as defined in TS 38.211 [8]) to zero for PTAG;
B1838: 3>indicate to lower layers a Differential Koffset with value zero.
B1839: 2>allow uplink transmission on the Serving Cell.
B1840: 1>if an indication of uplink synchronization loss is received from upper layers (see clause 5.2.2.6 and 5.7.19 of TS 38.331 [5]):
B1841: 2>if uplink synchronization loss is due to satellite switch with re-synchronization (see clause 5.7.19 of TS 38.331 [5]):
B1842: 3>not perform any uplink transmission on the Serving Cell.
B1843: 2>else:
B1844: 3>flush all HARQ buffers;
B1845: 3>not perform any uplink transmission on the Serving Cell.
B1846: NOTE:The MAC entity suspends all UL operations (e.g. stop RACH, SR, and UL HARQ operation) after receiving the indication of an uplink synchronization loss and resumes the operation when receiving an indication of uplink synchronization.
B1847: 5.2bMaintenance of UL Synchronization for CLTM candidate cell
B1848: The MAC entity shall for each CLTM candidate cell:
B1849: 1>when an LTM Candidate Timing Advance Command MAC CE described in clause 6.1.3.4b is received:
B1850: 2>if two TAGs are configured for the CLTM candidate cell:
B1851: 3>store the TA value in the LTM Candidate Timing Advance Command MAC CE for the indicated CLTM candidate cell for the indicated TAG as specified in clause 6.1.3.4b;
B1852: 3>start or restart the ltm-TimeAlignmentTimer or ltm-TimeAlignmentTimerTag2 associated with the indicated LTM candidate cell for the indicated TAG as specified in clause 6.1.3.4b;
B1853: 2>else:
B1854: 3>store the TA value in the LTM Candidate Timing Advance Command MAC CE for the indicated CLTM candidate cell as specified in clause 6.1.3.4b;
B1855: 3>start or restart the ltm-TimeAlignmentTimer associated with the indicated LTM candidate cell as specified in clause 6.1.3.4b.
B1856: NOTE:If the UE receives more TA values than it can store, it is up to the UE implementation which TA values to store or discard.
B1857: 1>when the CLTM candidate configuration(s) or all execution condition(s) for a CLTM candidate configuration is released as specified in TS 38.331 [5]:
B1858: 2>stop the running ltm-TimeAlignmentTimer(s) and ltm-TimeAlignmentTimerTag2(s) associated with the corresponding CLTM candidate cell(s), if any;
B1859: 2>release the stored TA value for the corresponding CLTM candidate cell(s), if any.
B1860: 5.3DL-SCH data transfer
B1861: 5.3.1DL Assignment reception
